Studio Belmont Homepage Revamp
description:
Hi team,

The client has requested a revamp of their homepage. Please create a test page for this task.
Canva file: https://www.canva.com/design/DAG9lfB1yHQ/LEDEcSf-B3SH5SPdtdML_Q/edit

Here are the major key points for this revamp:

1. Header / Hero Section

  • Each slide should support:

  • A unique image
  • Unique headline and supporting text per slide (previously image-only)
  • A unique CTA button link per slide

  • Animation:

  • Reduce the image expand/zoom animation duration to 1 second
  • Current animation causes pixelation and prevents full image detail from being visible

  • Navigation cue:

  • Add a down-arrow indicator that scrolls users to the next section
  • Reference behavior/style: https://sandiegohardware.com/

2. Image Treatment

  • All hero images should be full-bleed (edge-to-edge, no padding or gutters)

3. “Explore What’s New” Section

  • Each entry should link directly to its corresponding product detail page

4. Featured Product Copy

  • This should have the ability to input a link that leads to a collection

5. New & Featured Collections Section

  • This should have the ability to input a link that leads to a collection

6. Join the Trade Program Section

  • The current CTA redirect points to an outdated page
  • PM to coordinate with Jerry to confirm the correct destination before finalizing the link

7. Development Workflow Notes

  • Please build and deliver section by section / component by component so the client can review and provide feedback incrementally
  • Feel free to introduce UI/UX refinements that elevate the homepage look and feel, with the goal of making it more premium and luxurious, as long as core requirements above are met

Let me know if you have any questions or concerns. Thank you!

name: Newsletter Update
description:
Hi team,

Here is a development request related to the client’s newsletter flow.

Current Setup

At the moment, the client creates a blog post that is published on the website:
https://www.maxtonvalve.com/newsletter

However, they would also like this same content to be sent to their customers via the newsletter module.


Requested Development
  1. New Content Type
    1. Create a new content type, ideally labeled Press Release & Newsletter.

    2. This content type should closely mimic the existing Blog posting flow.
  2. Newsletter Integration
    1. Within the Blog/Press Release posting, there should be a clear and easy way for the client to send the blog post link through the newsletter.
    2. We can further discuss the best and most user-friendly approach for this implementation.

Additional Newsletter Requests

Sign-Up Automation
  • When a new member signs up and is approved, and they have checked “Subscribe to newsletter”:

    • They should be added to the newsletter list based on the Company Name they entered.

    • If the company matches Otis, Schindler, Kone, or TK Elevator, they should be added to the corresponding list.
    • If they do not fall under any of these, they should be added to the Independent list.

description:
Hi Erica Inocian ,

Please see this request from the client regarding a series of blog posts that they are planning. Please share the best course of action for this. Do we just use these topics as upcoming blog posts for their website or is there a much better approach that could benefit the client?


So our ultimate goal with this blog (or series of blogs) would be to increase applicant volume, while improving candidate quality.  We think that SEO driven content could have a meaningful impact on our success with our hiring goals/needs.  I am thinking we should focus on a more job-seeker driven content that can get our name out to those seeking local security positions as their line of work.
A few things we would like this to lean into:
  • Search intent: People actively looking for security jobs (particularly when searching local or the "near me" searches)
  • Positioning: Clear differentiation from typical security companies: structured, professional, and growth-oriented, maybe include culture since it is a pretty big factor for us
  • Conversion: Content should naturally guide candidates toward applying, not just something made to inform
Some things we could highlight are:
  • Professional environment vs. “warm body” staffing
  • Consistency (hours, expectations, leadership)
  • Growth path into supervisory roles
  • Real support and accountability in the field
You are the SEO expert, so I would ask you what you would know to have the most impact on SEO between looking at a single blog vs a series of blogs in this realm.  Below is something I pulled together as a general idea of the way I was thinking we approach a blog (Kyle or Jason may have a different take on this).  

Security Guard Jobs in Michigan: What to Expect & How to Get Started
If you’re searching for work in the security industry, you’ve likely come across a wide range of job listings with varying pay rates, schedules, and expectations.  What isn’t always clear, however, is what the role actually looks like on the daily, or how to identify a company that treats security as a professional role rather than simply filling shifts.
The following is a guide that breaks down what to expect, how to get started and what to look for before you apply.
What Does a Security Guard Actually Do?
At a basic level, security guards are responsible for keeping people, property, and environments safe.  But the reality of the job depends heavily on the company and the site.
Typical responsibilities include:
  • Monitoring cameras and activity on site
  • Conducting foot patrols and checking access points
  • Writing detailed daily and incident reports
  • Responding to disturbances or safety concerns
  • Communicating with residents, staff, or law enforcement when needed
In a strong operation, you’re not just “watching things,” you’re actively managing a site and preventing problems before they escalate.
Requirements to Become a Security Guard in Michigan
Getting started in Michigan is relatively straightforward, but there are still a few key requirements.
Most positions will require:
  • You to be at least 18 years old
  • A clean criminal background
  • Reliable transportation
  • Strong communication skills
What Most Job Listings Don’t Tell You
One of the biggest differences in security jobs isn’t the title, it’s the company behind it.
Some companies operate with very little structure.  That can mean:
  • Inconsistent scheduling
  • Limited training
  • Little to no supervision
  • Being left on your own to figure things out
Others take a more professional approach, where expectations are clear and support is built in.
Before applying, it’s worth asking:
  • Is there consistent leadership and supervision?
  • Are expectations clearly defined?
  • Is training provided, or are you expected to learn on your own?
  • Is this a long-term role, or just coverage for open shifts?
These factors will shape your every day experience more than anything else.
What a Strong Security Role Should Offer
If you’re looking for more than just a temporary job, there are a few things that set better companies apart:
Consistency
Reliable hours and clear expectations.
Structure
Defined procedures, reporting standards, and communication channels.
Support
Supervisors who are involved, responsive, and actually present in the field.
Growth Opportunities
A path to move into leadership roles like supervisor or operations support.  Security can be a long-term career, but only if the company is built that way.
A Day in the Life of a Security Officer
While every site is different, most shifts follow a structured routine:
  • Start of shift: equipment check, site overview, and pass-down from previous officer (if applicable)
  • Active monitoring: cameras, foot patrols, and resident or staff interaction
  • Incident response: addressing issues as they come up and documenting them clearly
  • End of shift: reporting and communication for the next officer (if applicable)
The job requires attention to detail, professionalism, and the ability to stay consistent, even during slower periods.

How to Apply for Security Guard Jobs Near You
When you’re ready to apply, focus on companies that clearly outline:
  • Job expectations
  • Scheduling and hours
  • Training and onboarding
  • Opportunities for advancement
Look beyond the job title and pay rate, those don’t always tell the full story.
Looking for a Security Role with Structure and Growth?
At Grey Dog Security, we focus on building a professional security team, not just filling shifts.
Our officers work in structured environments with:
  • Clear expectations and schedules posted a month in advance
  • Active supervision and support
  • Ongoing training and development
  • Opportunities to grow into leadership roles
If you’re looking for a role where you can build experience and grow, we encourage you to apply.
